Delicious Sausage and Bacon Soup

~4 cups water

~4 cups (2 cans) chicken/turkey broth.

8 ounce Bacon (or more)

1 lb Italian sausage (Jimmy Dean style acceptable alternative)

2 Large Potatoes (1-1.5lbs)

1 Medium Onion (or large, can't have too much)

2 Cloves Garlic (I'll use 2-3 bulbs. It's impossible to add too much)

1 cup Heavy Cream (added at very end)

2 cups chopped kale or swiss chard (added at very end)

Salt/pepper to taste

Extras - To Taste (Optional):

Chicken Bouillon

Sage

Bay leaves

Chives

Parsley

Etc

Directions

1) Bring Water & Chicken broth to simmer over Medium Heat.

2) Dice Potatoes/Onions. Mince or Crush Garlic. Add to broth.

3) Cut and Cook Bacon & Sausage (separate). Add once potatoes start to soften.

4) Simmer for another ~10 minutes after bacon/sausage added. Do Not Boil.

5) Add Kale (or Chard) and Cream. Bring back up to temperature.

6) Salt/Pepper to taste. Ready to serve

X) Add "Extra" seasoning anytime, preferably near beginning.

Directions (Condensed)

1) Simmer Water/Broth on Medium Heat (Do not Boil)

2) Add Veggies/Seasonings

3) Cook Bacon/Sausage. Add once potatoes start to soften.

4) Simmer for another 10 minutes

5) Add Kale/Cream - Bring back to simmer.

6) Salt/Pepper/Serve

I read about a study some time ago that clarified the results and findings of the Stanford Marshmallow Experiment by showing that some of the differences observed in delaying instant gratification stems from the socioeconomic level and mean home income of the participant.

Low income participants were less able to delay instant gratification as this is associated with being uncertain as to where your next meal is coming from. Participants from low income families were also less likely to have performed well at school or work in followup too.

High income participants on the other hand were always certain about where their meals were coming from and found it easier to delay the instant gratification of a quick snack. Greater financial support and more present parents also contributed to higher attainment at school and in careers during followup.
